script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saying Tyre doesn't mourn at all goes beyond what the verse says about its reaction.
The text does not say Tyre isn't scared, and the explanation states that feeling as fact.
God answered Tyre, but the passage doesn't say He answered right away.
The passage doesn't say Tyre's walls are the first thing to go.
Identifying Sennacherib as king of Assyria is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs its own reference.
Identifying Cyrus as king of Persia is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs its own reference.
The passage says Nebuchadnezzar will build a ramp and raise shields, but it doesn't say these are how he gets close.
The verse doesn't mention anyone climbing the walls, but it doesn't establish that nobody does.
The verse says the walls will shake from the noise, not that they will shake from noise alone.
The verse says the walls will shake from the noise, not that they will shake from noise alone.
The passage says stones, timber and soil will be thrown into the water. It doesn't say the walls and homes in their entirety will end up there.
The passage doesn't say everything that made up Tyre will go into the sea. It names stones, timber and soil.
The passage describes what the princes will do, but doesn't say they aren't sailing anywhere.
A quiet room is an invented setting, and the passage says the princes will lament.
Calling Tyre a city that ruled the water goes beyond the lament's description of her as powerful on the sea.
Comparing Tyre's destruction and disappearance to a cookie box at a party makes light of a prophecy involving slaughter and suffering.
The passage says Tyre will be sought but never found. It doesn't say the search goes on.
